title: Who’s on the other side
desc: The players you trade against, and your real edge

cards.title: Who sold you those shares?
cards.situation: You buy 10 shares of a company in your app. Someone sold them to you. Who?

options.feedback: The company sold its shares long ago, when it first listed. Today you buy from someone who already owns them.
Your app only passes your order on. The shares come from someone who already owns them and wants to sell.

options.text: Another trader, a fund or a market maker
options.feedback: Every trade has two sides. When you buy, someone else sells, and they often have more money and data than you.
Buying doesn’t create shares. Someone who already owns them has to sell them to you.

cards.title: Meet the players
cards.text: Tap each one, from [[market-maker|market makers]] to funds, to see their edge and your move.

steps.label: Market makers
steps.sub: Always quote a buy and a sell price.
steps.edge: Earn the spread, see order flow.
steps.move: Pay as little spread as you can (Lesson 4).

steps.label: Institutions (funds, banks)
steps.move: You’re small, so you get in and out instantly.

steps.label: High-frequency traders
steps.sub: Trade in thousandths of a second.
steps.edge: Speed: they react before you see the news.
steps.move: Don’t chase tiny moves in seconds. Hold longer.

steps.label: Long-term investors
steps.move: Borrow their patience: hold your best ideas longer.

steps.label: Other app traders
steps.move: Have a plan and stick to it.

cards.title: Your real edge
cards.text: You won’t out-speed the robots or out-research a hedge fund. Your real edges are **patience**, **flexibility** and **picking only the trades you understand**.

blocks.tip: A small trader can sit in cash for a month. A **$10B fund usually can’t**: it’s paid to stay invested.

cards.title: Who wins this fight?
cards.q: Drag each fight into the right box.
items: Waiting a month for the right setup

you: Waiting a month for the right setup

itemFeedback.Reacting to news in 0.001 seconds: A robot reacts in 0.001 seconds; your thumb needs about 0.3. That’s 300 times slower. Don’t race it.
itemFeedback.Reading 500 reports on one company: Funds pay whole teams to read every report. Research is their fight.
itemFeedback.Waiting a month for the right setup: A big fund must stay invested. You can sit in cash for a month. That edge is yours.

cards.right: Speed and research belong to them. Patience and small size belong to you. Pick fights in your box.

cards.title: Big news just dropped
cards.q: The price jumps in 0.1 seconds. You see the news 5 seconds later. What’s your best move?

options.text: Buy now, before it rises more
options.feedback: Robots moved the price in 0.1 seconds. Chasing it means buying from them, late. Your edge is patience, not speed.

options.text: Don’t chase it. Stick to your plan
options.feedback: The robots already moved the price. Sticking to your plan keeps you out of a race you can’t win.

options.text: Ask a friend at the company what’s next
options.feedback: Trading on secret company information is insider trading. It’s illegal, and never an edge you can use.
Panic selling on news you saw late is chasing too, just the other way. Your edge is patience, not speed.

cards.headline: You know who you trade against, and where you can win.
lines: Every trade has someone on the other side, often with more money and data.
Don’t fight robots on speed or funds on research.
Your edge: patience, flexibility and picking only the trades you understand.
